newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Cricket-Sri Lanka tipped to win Asia Cup.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Sri Lanka tipped to win Asia Cup.

text.p: World champions Sri Lanka are favourites to beat India and take the Asia Cup for only the second time in its history on Saturday.
But the toss and weather will play an important role in the match to be played at Colombo's R. Premadasa stadium.
The meterological department has forecast occasional showers with sunny intervals for Saturday and both teams will be praying that the skies remain clear.
Sri Lanka lost to India in the 1994 Singer Cup final in Colombo when the match was reduced to 25 overs a side due to rain.
India's confidence was boosted on Thursday by their nine-wicket win over Bangladesh, that enabled them to knock Pakistan out of competition on a better run rate.
"The final against Sri Lanka is very important. The victory over Bangladesh has definitely put us in the right frame of mind," said Indian captain Sachin Tendulkar.
"It's not going to be an easy match. I think Sri Lanka has got a very good record at R. Premadasa Stadium. We've got to see whether we can hopefully stop that," he said.
Sri Lanka beat India by six wickets in the league stage of the competition at this venue. The defeat exposed the limitations of the Indian bowling attack.
"I think you will have to leave our bowlers alone and let them play without any pressure. All they need is the support from everybody. I am sure they will do wonders," said Tendulkar.
The Indian captain credited his bowlers for their win over Bangladesh on Thursday. Medium-pacer Robin Singh was singled out for deliveries that brought him three wickets for 13 runs in nine overs.
"We were not particular who came into the final. Our policy is to play positive cricket like we have been doing throughout and go out and win," said Sri Lanka captain Arjuna Ranatunga.
Sri Lanka boast one of the strongest batting line-ups in one-day cricket with batsmen like Sanath Jayasuriya, Aravinda de Silva and the skipper himself.
Sri Lanka last the Asia Cup in 1986 in Colombo. But on that occasion India did not play.
The last three Asia Cup finals held in Dhaka (1988), Calcutta (1990) and Sharjah (1995) have seen India get the better of Sri Lanka.

Teams: SRI LANKA (from): Arjuna Ranatunga (captain), Sanath Jayasuriya, Mavan Atapattu, Aravinda de Silva, Roshan Mahanama, Lanka de Silva, Kumara Dharmasena, Ruwan Kalpage, Chaminda Vaas, Muthiah Muralitharan, Sajeeva de Silva, Upul Chandana.

INDIA (from): Sachin Tendulkar (captain), Saurav Ganguly, Navjot Sidhu, Mohammad Azharuddin, Rahul Dravid, Saba Karim, Robin Singh, Ajay Jadeja, Anil Kumble, Venkatesh Prasad, Abey Kuruvila, Noel David.
